        Hard figures that hundreds of persons have spotted
  the monster, but have been reluctant to report it.
        "They're afraid of ridicule," he says.
        But Pa'tch t'alks about his experience with the      I



  "monster" in no uncertain terms.
        "By Judas priest! I saw that thing," he says.
        He and his wife were sharing a picnic lunch on May
  20, 1960, when it surfaced off the Champlain Islands
 along the lake's western shore, he says.
        "We were there for a half hour, eating our lunch
  and watching that critter," Patch says.                 __
        "It was definitely sriaKe-hke in form. I could see
  three or four humps up in the air, but they were verti-
  cal - and not lying horizontally along the water like a
  snake's would. ·
        "It was right there on top of the water," he says.
  "Just enjoying a swim."
        Sometimes it would lift its head out of the water a
  couple of feet, then "continue on its leisurely way."
        The Patches watched with fascination, also through
  binoculars, as the creature "slowly turned and started
  working back toward the area from which it came."
        Patch agrees with Hard that fear of ridicule has
  held down the number of reported monster sightings.
        "People are very disinclined to believe anything
  like that unless they see it with their very awn eyes,"
  hesay~                                          ·
